title: 3-minute incident narrative for sellers — rapid script & battlecard
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, 3-minute narrative and speaker-script sellers can use when a customer reports a live inference incident (latency spikes / errors / model degradation). Primary goal is to buy time, reduce customer anxiety, provide a clear next step, and avoid overpromising technical fixes in the moment.

How to use: quick read before hopping on call or before sending a first Slack/Email. Keep it conversational — sellers are not engineers; this is a de-risking script.

One-sentence framing for the customer (first line):
"Thanks — we see where you’re coming from. We have an internal playbook and an on-call runbook; I’m escalating this to our SRE & Solutions teams and will follow up with a triage summary in 30–60 minutes. In the meantime, here’s what I can do right now to keep your app safe."

30-second script (what to say on the first call):
- Acknowledge and empathize: "I’m really sorry for the disruption — I know this impacts your users."
- Quick reassure: "We have a dedicated incident flow for inference issues; I’ve already opened a triage ticket and looped our SRE and Solutions engineers."
- Near-term actions: "We can temporarily route requests to a compatible, lower-latency model variant, enable the cached prefix we discussed, or shift traffic to a different region while we investigate. Which would you prefer us to try first?"
- Commitment: "I’ll get you an initial update in 30 minutes and a remediation plan within 4 hours unless we have it sooner."

Suggested immediate actions (seller-level, non-technical options):
- Ask whether there’s a safe time window to test fallbacks (off-peak helps).
- Offer to switch to a predefined fallback model (name the variant used in the pilot) — make this an opt-in config change you can implement with the support team.
- Offer rate limiting or short-circuit responses (e.g., canned fallback text) to preserve UX while SRE investigates.
- Commit to a follow-up report with metrics we’ll capture (error type, P50/P95 latency, impacted endpoints).

Default fallback options (what to propose if customer needs instant mitigation):
1) Model variant fallback: route to the verified LLM-compact-qa-v1 (lower latency, slightly different quality profile).
2) Region reroute: shift traffic to eu-west-1 / us-west-2 if the customer is region-flexible.
3) Cache short-circuit: return cached responses for the top X queries or degrade to summary-only output.
4) Throttle + graceful degrade: reduce concurrency for their API key to maintain stability.

Escalation matrix (who we loop, and suggested wording to the customer):
- Level 1 (immediate): Solutions Eng (Riley Chen) + On-call SRE (paging via #sre-oncall). Tell customer: "I’ve looped engineering and SRE and they’re triaging now."
- Level 2 (if L1 needs hands-on): Platform Eng lead (Samira Holt) + Runtime Eng (PR assigned). Tell customer: "We’re doing a deeper runtime inspection and will share a technical snapshot."
- Level 3 (if RCA needed / contractual impact): Account Exec + Customer Success + Legal/Contracts. Tell customer: "We’ll prepare an incident summary and any contractual impact assessment."

Slack / email snippets (copy-paste templates):
- To #sre-oncall: "INCIDENT: {customer} experiencing inference errors / high latency on route {route}. First report at {time}. Requesting triage. Customer contact: {seller}. Link: {jira}."
- To customer (initial): "Thanks for flagging this — we’re on it. I’ve escalated to SRE and Solutions Eng and will update you in 30 minutes. If you prefer we attempt a temporary fallback (model/regional), say the word and I’ll kick it off."

Customer questions & suggested answers (seller-friendly):
Q: How long until it’s fixed?
A: We’ll send an initial triage update in ~30 minutes and a plan within 4 hours. If we can remediate faster we will.

Q: Will you lose my data?
A: No — customer data and requests are preserved; we may route to a safe variant but not drop data.

Q: Is this likely to be a billing impact?
A: Not at first — we’ll confirm if there are cost/regression implications after triage.

Talking points on SLAs & risk (short):
- If customer has Reserved/Dedicated capacity, prioritize invoking the Dedicated fallback/pool.
- If hosted tier: offer a documented temporary throttle or model downgrade with tracking until SRE confirms stability.
- For Enterprise customers, loop post-sales CSM immediately for SLA expectations.

Quick numbers sellers can use (calibrated language):
- "We aim to provide an initial triage update in ~30 minutes and a remediation plan in under 4 hours for production-impacting incidents."
- "Common mitigations (fallback model, cache short-circuit, region reroute) typically restore acceptable service in minutes to a few hours depending on scope."

Redlines — what not to promise:
- Don’t promise a root cause or exact timeline beyond the initial update window.
- Don’t commit to code-level fixes or DB-level rollbacks yourself.
- Don’t give out internal incident severity labels (we’ll share a customer-facing severity).

Quick diagnostics sellers can collect (helps triage):
- When did the issue start? Which endpoints/routes?
- % of requests failing vs timing out. Example error messages or sample payloads (copy-paste).
- Any recent client-side changes or config changes on their side?

Post-incident deliverable checklist (seller & CSM owner):
- Consolidated timeline + key metrics (latency P50/P95, error rate) — target: within 24–48 hours.
- Mitigation summary (what fallback was used and when).
- Customer impact assessment and next steps (RCA timeline).

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Need a lightweight UI toggle in Console for sellers to trigger the model fallback (tracked: CONSOLE-439).
- Verify canonical fallback model names and quality deltas for customer-facing comparisons.
- Draft a one-page incident summary template for postmortems (owner: Miguel).

Related artifacts & references:
- Incident playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/incident-playbook
- Example triage ticket: JIRA-INF-9876
- Runtime PR that added region routing flags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842

Notes / voice / tone guidance for sellers:
- Keep it short. Use active verbs (escalated, triaging, have looped).
- Avoid engineering jargon; use "triage" not "root cause analysis" in early stages.
- Be transparent about timelines and follow-up cadence.

Quick checklist (two-line version to memorize):
1) Acknowledge + escalate (I’ve looped SRE & Solutions).
2) Offer immediate mitigations (fallback model / cache / region).
3) Commit to update in 30 minutes + plan in 4 hours.

— End of deck sketch —

Notes to product: we should convert this into a one-click agent in Console (pre-populated incident message + fallback actions) so sellers can trigger mitigations without requiring manual triage. Filing feature request under CONSOLE-439.

-- author notes: draft, use as seller cheatcard for Q1 enablement. Contains rough timing and names — confirm on-call roster before publish.
